metadata.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence Models in Educational Analytics and Decision Making: A Systematic Review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a systematic review (PRISMA-based) that synthesizes findings from 70 included quantitative studies rather than analyzing a single ILSA micro-dataset. Because no student-level assessment dataset (e.g., PISA/TIMSS) is pooled and re-scaled within this review, there is no defined sampling frame, no PV generation, and no survey-weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply at the review level. The included primary studies may use survey weights depending on their data source, but the review does not report a unified weighting scheme or replicate-weight approach. Therefore, weighting guidance for international large-scale assessments cannot be operationalized from this manuscript alone; readers must consult each included study’s methods for weight usage and complex-survey handling.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a systematic review that does not estimate student-level cognitive achievement scores from ILSA-style plausible values (PVs). The manuscript reports bibliographic counts and qualitative synthesis of AI-model usage across included studies, so PV generation/combining rules are not part of the review’s methodology. Missing-data handling is also not specified because the review does not re-analyze microdata; it only screens and summarizes eligible studies.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Systematic review selection: searches conducted in September 2021 for articles published between January 2000 and September 2021. Inclusion criteria required English-language scholarly articles/reviews focused on basic education (primary/secondary/high school) and using AI models for academic performance evaluation/prediction, with eligibility limited to titles/abstracts keywords and then full-text availability. Exclusions removed non-English works, pre-2000 publications, studies outside basic education (e.g., higher education, extracurricular courses, MOOC), studies unrelated to academic performance, and non-peer-reviewed or conference/book-chapter items. The review further used Rayyan® for independent screening by two authors with a third reviewer resolving disagreements, and applied PRISMA flow to derive the final set of 70 included articles.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict predicting or classifying basic-education performance (primary/secondary/high sc, finding that This PRISMA-based systematic review (World 2023, 4:288–313) searched multiple databases (ERIC, IEEE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science) using PICO-defined criteria focused on AI models predicting or classifying basic-education performance (primary/secondary/high school) from 2000 to September 2021. From 19,114 initial references, duplicates were removed (13,847 screened by title/abstract), 182 were read in full, and 70 studies met inclusion criteria. The review reports descriptive synthesis rather than a single predictive model: publication trends peaked in 2020 (27 studies), Portugal had the most dataset-origin-related articles (14), and the most common study goals were model comparison (N=34) and education performance forecasting (N=36). Across included studies, decision trees and neural networks were frequently used, and only 31.4% (N=22) explicitly discussed translating results into public policy. Limitations include the absence of a unified dataset, no re-estimation of performance metrics across studies, and no standardized treatment of weighting or missing data at the review level. data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is intentionally sparse for ILSA/ML-analytic fields because the manuscript is a systematic review rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis. It does not train or evaluate a single ML model on a defined student-level dataset, and it does not report PV handling, missing-data procedures, or per-country student sample sizes for an original analysis. Consequently, fields such as main_findings (StructuredFinding rows), ml_techniques, and confounders_identified are empty by design.
